agree.reason: The 20-mile chain gap, the July 1 renewal deadline and the offer of invoices and a meeting make a concrete case that a skeptical benefits director could act on, though it never turns the loss into a dollar figure she would feel.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'third will close' claim, but 'a fifth of its work at a loss' and 'every pharmacy still open is now losing money' go further than the facts, which show an average loss on the top 20 generics only, with possible brand-name offsets; the list of members' jobs is also invented.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives no figures: there is no estimate of yearly loss from 3,100 prescriptions at $1.80 and no closure pace from 9 in two years, and 22% is only restated as 'one in five'.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately, as members driving more than 20 miles to a chain in 14 counties, and notes the nine closures without claiming they were caused by rates.

qualification.reason: 'If nothing changes' is tied to no date or threshold the reader can check, though the July 1 renewal and the May 1 meeting window give some anchor.

objections.reason: It answers 'members have chains' with the 20-mile fact and 'they complain every year' with the invoice offer, but leaves open the obvious reply that losses on generics may be offset by brand-name margins.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter with a clear ask and a signature that suits both the plan and the newspapers.
